title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS)
qa: Which TOS type is most common? Neurogenic.
Why is a positive Adson test alone weak evidence? Pulse reduction occurs in many people without symptoms.
What is an emergency in TOS? Signs of venous thrombosis or arterial occlusion.
What should you rule out in a smoker with shoulder pain and a drooping eyelid? Pancoast tumour.
Why use sliders before tensioners? Sliders move the nerve with less tension, so they are less provocative.

fields.Purpose: Reproduce symptoms with sustained overhead position
fields.Patient position: Sitting or standing, shoulders abducted to 90 degrees and externally rotated, elbows bent to 90 degrees ("hands up" position)
fields.Action: Patient slowly opens and closes the hands for up to 3 minutes
fields.Positive: Reproduction of the patient's arm symptoms, heaviness or inability to continue

fields.Position: Sitting, arm by the side; therapist palpates the radial pulse
fields.Action: Patient extends the neck, rotates toward the tested side, takes a deep breath and holds it
fields.Positive: Reduction of the pulse with reproduction of symptoms
fields.Limits: Pulse change occurs in many healthy people; symptom reproduction matters more

redFlags.Finding: Sudden arm swelling and blue colour
Cold, white, painful fingers, absent pulse
Smoker with shoulder pain, Horner signs, weight loss

manualNotes: First rib mobilisation (caudal glide) when the first rib is elevated and stiff: supine or sitting, therapist's hand on the first rib above the clavicle, gentle downward glide.
Gentle scalene and pectoralis minor soft-tissue work for comfort.
Neural mobilisation using sliders, not tensioners, if irritable (Vol 13 Ch 5).

exercise.Exercise: Scapular elevation and upward rotation (shrugs with arms slightly abducted, wall slides)
Pectoralis minor stretch in a doorway

exerciseNotes: Activity modification: avoid prolonged overhead work and heavy shoulder bags; sleep with arms below shoulder level.
modalityNotes: Not routinely indicated. Heat for comfort.
